A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FaceLift. Their complete main texts and appendices, including readable tables, figures and equations, support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Cafca and Ava-256 evaluations in Tables 1–2, qualitative reconstructions, ablations and video demonstrations.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and adds comparator results, quantitative component ablations and demonstrations of an autoregressive video extension.

M1.justification: V1 reconstructs video frames independently. V2 adds an autoregressive deformation pipeline with an eight-layer MLP predicting Gaussian position, opacity and scale changes, supervised by subsequent-frame renderings (supplementary Section 3.5). This is a substantial procedural extension. Input-view reconstruction and object pretraining followed by head fine-tuning were already present in v1.

E1.justification: The underlying training datasets, Cafca, Ava-256, real and cartoon portraits, and video reconstruction remain. V2 removes the explicit image-plus-driving-video reenactment demonstration using LivePortrait from v1 Section 4.5/Figure 9. The larger portrait galleries mostly redistribute existing examples rather than establish new coverage.

E2.justification: Cafca comparisons add GGHead, Dual Encoder and Our MV + LGM; Ava-256 adds Our MV + LGM. Supplementary Table 3 adds TRELLIS, Unique3D and InstantMesh, while Figure 22 evaluates fine-tuned LGM. These substantially broaden evaluated comparators. RodinHD and DimensionX comparisons already existed.

E3.justification: Shared aligned benchmark identities, camera lists, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged. V2 removes the unaligned 30-view Cafca evaluation and adds settings for new controls, including a 20-degree target elevation and eight-view reconstruction. Reconstructor sampling changes from 32 HDR renderings to either 32 ambient or 25 HDR renderings in supplementary Section 5.2; this reported revision does not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative input-view reconstruction and multi-view attention ablations, a reconstructor without object pretraining, an eight-view alternative, and LGM integration/fine-tuning analyses. These investigate previously untested component contributions and transfer behavior. The lighting ablation is retained in the supplement, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's additional result tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Shared aligned benchmark scores are unchanged, including FaceLift PSNR of 16.61 on Cafca and 16.52 on Ava-256. V2 adds substantial comparator and ablation results: supplementary Table 4 reports ArcFace distances of 0.2367 without input reconstruction and 0.2126 without attention, versus 0.1573 for the full model. Unaligned Cafca results disappear, and autoregressive video results are added.

T1.justification: V2 supplementary Section 4.1 adds a formal joint multi-view diffusion formulation, forward/reverse Markov factorizations, Gaussian transition definitions and a noise-prediction objective (Equations 6–10). This is a limited mathematical addition to v1's descriptive treatment, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 makes input-view reconstruction and two-stage reconstructor training central to its generalization contribution, explicitly claims benchmark construction, and strengthens generalization to 'no domain gap' in the introduction. V1's abstract-level video and reenactment claims disappear. These changes substantially redefine the contribution framing despite retaining the principal reconstruction claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds mechanism explanations connecting input reconstruction to reduced synthetic overfitting and object pretraining to geometric diversity. It interprets the eight-view tradeoff and failed LGM fine-tuning, and adds limitations involving blurred unseen regions and excessively dark rear hair. Earlier accessory and out-of-distribution limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents the 50-degree field of view and MTCNN resizing/cropping procedure, an approximately eight-second inference breakdown, attention/transformer implementation details, and the deformation network. These improve technical disclosure; most existing training hyperparameters, hardware information and the project-page address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Morphable Diffusion and HeadGAP, citations to SynthLight and LPFF, and literature supporting the expanded comparators. LivePortrait and Instant-NSR-PL references disappear. The broader positioning around synthetic heads, diffusion and large reconstruction models remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around generalization. Ablations become a separate main section, real-image inference receives its own subsection, and lighting/video material moves into a substantially reorganized supplement. This exceeds localized language editing.

P2.justification: V2 revises the pipeline diagram, restructures comparison figures and tables, expands ablation displays, and adds mesh-comparison and autoregressive-deformation illustrations. Existing portrait examples are regrouped into larger galleries, and benchmark camera tables are relocated together. These are substantial visual changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind FaceLift through dedicated face and mesh comparators, quantitative component ablations, and a pretraining control, addressing important gaps in v1's comparative and diagnostic support. Inference documentation and failure analysis also improve. Removing unaligned full-view Cafca results and asserting 'no domain gap' weaken balance, but the added evidence provides a substantial net quality gain.
